name: Tickets and RFC Hierarchy
purpose: Fix SR/RFC identity, hierarchy, relationship, Device Reference context, ticket-history and terminal-boundary ownership before import, Objectives and workbench LLDs consume them.

decisions.decision: Service Request is pivotal correlation context but not a universal aggregate parent; each domain keeps explicit ownership.
Direct SR↔RFC links terminate only at root/master RFCs; subordinate context is inherited with provenance.
RFC hierarchy is a relationship-derived two-level one-parent acyclic forest with no arbitrary subordinate-count business cap.
RFC Customer is zero-or-one current canonical Customer; resolved branch members must agree while unresolved ownership stays explicit.
RFC may directly own Device Reference context without an SR; subordinate RFCs may have distinct Device References. Network Element resolution never replaces the RFC→DeviceReference relationship.
SR/RFC link changes are lifecycle-neutral, history-preserving and idempotent at duplicate/absent boundaries.
Accepted terminal RFC evidence is separate from the reviewed local cascade; downstream Task/Objective/Communication effects occur only through the confirmed cascade command.
RFC archive/restore is reversible local presentation state; exact source reconciliation continues while archived.
WFM hierarchy context is derived solely from the owning RFC hierarchy; Tickets does not create a second WFM hierarchy.
Working Notes are SOMA-owned ticket history and protected from source-import overwrite.

unresolved_here_by_design: exact SR/RFC table/index layout and local-ID allocator implementation
exact RFC hierarchy query/materialized projection strategy
exact terminal-cascade transaction participant interfaces delegated across HLD-06/HLD-10/HLD-14
